title: Atlas Banking — POC Audit Answers & Evidence Appendix
body:
Executive summary:
This appendix contains our consolidated answers to Atlas Banking's security questionnaire for the September 2025 POC, plus a curated evidence index and workshop notes. The intention is to: (1) provide direct answers the customer requested during the pre-POC risk review, (2) point to primary evidence artifacts, and (3) capture workshop actions and outstanding mitigation items that affect the final deliverable for Dedicated and Private deployment options.

Scope and context:
- POC environment: Dedicated (reserved GPU) in us-east-1; optional Private VPC variant to be deployed in Atlas-managed cloud account for sensitive data processing tests.
- Data types for POC: synthetic customer records, hashed SSNs for matching tests, and model prompt logs scrubbed of PII. No production customer PII was ingested during initial runs.

Selected questionnaire Q&A (excerpted):
Q1: Where are customer inputs stored and how long are they retained?
A1: For Hosted: inputs are stored encrypted at rest in region-bound S3 buckets with lifecycle policy 30 days by default. For Dedicated/Private: inputs may be retained in tenant-dedicated storage controlled by the customer; default POC policy is 14 days. Retention policies for the POC were manually set to 7 days to limit exposure. Evidence: exhibit-1-retention-policy.txt (S3 path in linked_artifacts).

Q2: How is model cache (KV cache) protected from cross-tenant leakage?
A2: KV caches are isolated per tenant instance via process-level namespaces and strict GPU memory partitioning. We shadow tested with synthetic cross-tenant probes; results are in exhibit-4-kv-isolation-runbook.log.

Q3: Key management and rotation?
A3: Customer-encrypted volumes use KMS keys (AWS KMS or customer-provided keys via KMS proxy). Rotation is on a 90-day cadence by default; POC used a one-time rotation to validate procedures. Evidence: key-rotation-screenshot.png, KSM grant link in linked_artifacts.

Evidence index (primary exhibits):
- exhibit-1-retention-policy.txt — POC bucket lifecycle and policy export (S3).
- exhibit-2-network-architecture.png — simplified POC VPC diagram showing subnets, egress NATs, and security group mappings.
- exhibit-3-scan-results.html — static code scan summary for the inference runtime image used in the POC.
- exhibit-4-kv-isolation-runbook.log — results from synthetic cross-tenant KV isolation tests.
- exhibit-5-iam-audit.csv — IAM roles used by Dedicated instances with last-used timestamps.
- exhibit-6-obs-sample.json — sanitized observability sample showing token-level latency and redaction markers.

Data flow & controls summary:
- Ingress: API gateway in the customer region → Dedicated instance. TLS 1.2+ enforced; mTLS used for Private variant. Evidence: exhibit-2-network-architecture.png.
- At-rest: application storage and model artifacts encrypted with KMS-managed CMKs. Disk-level encryption enabled on all GPU instances.
- In-memory: sensitive attributes are redacted before being persisted; KV cache remains in RAM and is zeroed on process termination.
- Exfiltration controls: egress only allowed over approved endpoints; outbound firewall rules applied at subnet level.

Workshop notes (2025-09-26, recorded):
- Attendees: Atlas SecOps (M. Hwang, J. Ortega), Atlas Platform (R. Ali), Redwood SE (Maya Chen, Ethan Patel), Redwood SRE (Carlos Rivera).
- Key decisions: proceed with two-week Dedicated POC, then evaluate Private deployment for regulated workloads. Atlas requested an additional retention hardening and mandatory KMS BYOK for Private.
- Action items: (1) Provide BYOK integration guide (owner: Carlos Rivera, due 2025-10-07). (2) Create SOC2-mapped evidence bundle for Atlas procurement (owner: Lena Goldberg, due 2025-10-14). (3) Run cross-tenant KV fuzzing with larger corpus (owner: Ethan Patel, due 2025-10-10).

Risk register (highlights):
- R1: Temporary log misconfiguration could expose prompts. Mitigation: ensure redaction filter applied at the ingestion proxy; already patched in POC and verified (see exhibit-6-obs-sample.json).
- R2: Customer-managed keys misconfiguration during BYOK onboarding. Mitigation: onboarding checklist and pre-flight key validation runbook (linked in linked_artifacts).
- R3: Network egress to third-party analytics during evaluation. Mitigation: strict egress allowlist and packaging observability sinks within tenant VPC.

Compliance mapping snapshot (selected controls):
- Access control (SOC2 CC6): IAM least privilege roles applied; temporary credentials rotated for POC runs. Evidence: exhibit-5-iam-audit.csv.
- Encryption (SOC2 CC7): CMKs for data at rest; TLS enforcement for transit. Evidence: key-rotation-screenshot.png, network diagram.
- Change management (SOC2 CC10): POC image changes logged in GitHub PR with linked CI pipeline run (linked in linked_artifacts).

Next steps and timeline: 
- 2025-10-07: Deliver BYOK integration guide and sample Terraform for Atlas infra team.
- 2025-10-10: Complete extended KV isolation tests and publish results.
- 2025-10-14: Submit SOC2-aligned evidence package for procurement review (final deliverable).

Contacts: 
- Redwood SE lead: Maya Chen — maya.chen@redwood.ai — +1-415-555-0183
- Redwood SRE (BYOK): Carlos Rivera — carlos.rivera@redwood.ai
- Atlas SecOps primary: Min Hwang — min.hwang@atlasbank.com

Notes and provenance: 
- All exhibits referenced are stored under the S3 path listed in linked_artifacts. Sensitive artifacts (logs with PII) were redacted before upload; redaction markers are visible in exhibit-6-obs-sample.json. This appendix is intended for Atlas procurement and technical risk review; do not circulate externally without DLP approval.

Document history: created 2025-09-12 (initial draft), workshop updates 2025-09-26, evidence attachments refreshed 2025-10-03.
